thread:
sasha: Quick check — Galileo is asking for a Dedicated pool. Their baseline monthly committed is ~60,000 GPU-hours, but they have nightly batch scoring that produces short sharp tail spikes (5x sustained for ~20m). How aggressive should we be on commit vs burst? :thinking:
omar: Do we have a pattern for which region? will this be multi-region?
sasha: US-west primary, fallback to US-east. They prefer lower latency so main traffic stays west. Nightly jobs run in west too.
leila: If spikes are 20m @5x that's a short utilisation pattern. We usually size commit for steady-state p95 and rely on burst tokens for short tails. But need to confirm burst budget math and SLA tradeoffs.
jack: Can you share the raw numbers? concurrent GPUs at baseline vs during spike?
sasha: Baseline steady concurrency ~40 GPUs during peak. During nightly scoring it jumps to ~200 GPUs for those 20m windows. So extra ~= 160 GPUs for 20 minutes.
omar: Let's convert that to GPU-hours to compare to the 60k commit:
```
# rough calc
extra_gpu = 160
spike_minutes = 20
extra_gpu_hours_per_spike = extra_gpu * spike_minutes / 60
# = 160 * 20 / 60 = 53.333... GPU-hours per night
monthly_extra = extra_gpu_hours_per_spike * 30
# ~= 1600 GPU-hours/month
```
leila: So ~1.6k GPU-hours / month for spikes vs 60k commit => ~2.7% delta.
sasha: Right. But they want guarantees for that spike not to throttle. They asked about a buffer policy that won't blow their bill but ensures burst capacity.
jack: For Dedicated we can do: commit = 60k GPU-hours, plus a small reserved buffer (3–5%) pre-allocated for tail smoothing, and an on-demand burst pool for occasional >buffer events. That keeps committed cost predictable and gives a soft SLA for bursts.
omar: Operationally: two levers — "buffer reserve" (guaranteed across their pool) and "shared burst tokens" (cluster-level, fair-share). Buffer reserve buys predictability; shared burst is cheaper but not guaranteed.
leila: Agreed. Recommend default: buffer = 5% of commit for customers with regular nightly spikes. Also offer a "tail-burst add-on": pay-as-you-go excess billed at premium but with guaranteed pre-warm for X hours/day.
sasha: Can we quantify pre-warm cost and where it sits relative to their ask?
jack: Pre-warm for 160 GPUs * 20 minutes nightly = ~53 GPU-hours/day? Wait we did per night calc as 53 GPU-hours, monthly ~1.6k. If we pre-warm reserved buffer of 160 GPUs for 20m each night, that still counts to their committed hours unless we implement scheduled reservations (time-windowed reservations don't consume commit if specified as "ephemeral pre-warm" but we currently bill by GPU-hour consumed).
omar: Two options technically: 1) time-window reservations that we exclude from commit accounting (needs product approval), 2) bill all GPU-hours and offer discounted overage pricing for predictable tails. Option 1 reduces bill surprise but increases bookkeeping.
leila: For negotiation with Galileo, simpler is Option 2: keep commit = 60k, suggest 5% buffer (~3k GPU-hours), and rate-limit burst at a premium rate for excess. Show math: buffer covers most nights and protects SLA.
sasha: How to express buffer in UI? curve-based or flat headroom? I prefer an explicit "tail buffer" entry: X% pre-allocated, plus Y monthly burst hours at premium.
jack: Implementation notes for infra: need a scheduler hook that marks buffer VMs/GPU nodes as reserved for that tenant with fast preemption disabled. Also ensure KV cache warming is handled so cold-start latency doesn't kill the first few requests.
omar: Also watch cross-region bandwidth for fallback — if west runs out and we route to east, egress and latency costs rise. Add a routing policy: prefer local burst, then best-effort regional, then degrade to smaller model if still unavailable.
leila: Suggested defaults for sale doc: commit 60k GPU-hours, recommended tail buffer 5% (3k GPU-hours/month), burst pool paid at 2x hosted rate, scheduled pre-warm add-on available. Provide a small worked example in the quote.
sasha: I'll draft the quote language. Can someone sanity-check the SLA wording? "Guaranteed burst capacity up to buffer; additional burst best-effort with costed premium and failover policies"
jack: Sounds good. Add an explicit p99 latency SLA for primary region while on buffer, and a "best-effort" clause for excess bursts routed cross-region.
omar: infra-bot: scheduling note — created ticket INF-4821 to add tail-buffer metrics (p95/p99 burst width, nightly spike counter) and a dash tile for customer pages.
infra-bot: ticket INF-4821 created and assigned to @omar. ETA 2w.
leila: For billing, finance should show two line items: committed GPU-hours and burst premium usage. Keeps invoicing transparent.
sasha: Great. I'll share a draft quote with Galileo CSM and copy finance. Thanks all :thumbsup:
omar: one small follow up — do we need to recommend model quantization/shorter context during batch to reduce needed gpus? might reduce spike.
sasha: Good point. I'll ask Galileo if the nightly job can be batched or quantized. If they can drop memory per-inference we can shave GPUs.
jack: If they can use 4-bit quantization safely, GPUs required could drop ~30%, which would significantly lower burst sizing. Worth including as an optional reduction scenario in the quote.
leila: I'll add a line to the product spec: "Tail buffer both in % and abs GPU-hours + recommended model memory optimizations".
sasha: OK closing — I'll post the quote draft in #customer-success and drop a link here when ready. :eyes:
